title: 1.3 The scientific stack
description: Build reliable scientific Python workflows across labelled data, columnar query engines, statistical visualization, numerical computing, and reproducible exploration.
learningOutcomes: Construct schema-aware pandas and Polars pipelines with explicit indexing, join, null, ordering, and performance contracts
Create accessible Matplotlib and seaborn visualizations whose scales, estimators, distributions, and uncertainty are honest
Validate statistical, optimization, dense linear-algebra, and sparse numerical results with mathematical and computational diagnostics
Use Jupyter for reproducible exploration while production logic remains importable, tested, reviewable, and deployable

lessons.title: pandas: Series/DataFrame, indexing (loc/iloc), groupby-apply-agg, merges, reshaping (melt/pivot), time series, MultiIndex
lessons.description: Build reliable pandas pipelines by reasoning about labels, alignment, grouping, relational joins, shapes, time, and hierarchical indexes.
learningObjectives: Distinguish labels, positions, index alignment, and copy behavior
Build timezone-aware time-series and MultiIndex pipelines

lessons.title: polars — learn it after pandas; it's what you'll actually reach for on large data
lessons.description: Use Polars expressions, lazy query plans, Arrow-style columnar memory, streaming, and schema-aware validation for large analytical pipelines.
learningObjectives: Handle schemas, nulls, joins, groups, and windows

lessons.title: matplotlib: the Figure/Axes object model (not plt. state-machine style)
lessons.description: Create predictable visualizations by owning Figure, Axes, Artist, transform, layout, scale, and export decisions explicitly.
learningObjectives: Explain the Figure, Axes, Axis, and Artist hierarchy
Choose honest scales, limits, and transforms

lessons.title: seaborn for statistical plots
lessons.description: Use seaborn's semantic mappings and statistical estimators without hiding aggregation, uncertainty, sampling, or distribution shape.
learningObjectives: Choose honest distribution and relationship plots

lessons.title: scipy: stats, optimize, linalg, sparse
lessons.description: Use SciPy's statistical, optimization, linear-algebra, and sparse tools by making mathematical assumptions and numerical failure modes explicit.
learningObjectives: Select statistics from estimands and sampling design
Choose sparse formats and iterative solvers

lessons.title: Jupyter discipline: notebooks for exploration only, never for production logic
lessons.description: Use notebooks as reproducible exploration interfaces while moving tested, reusable, deployable logic into Python packages.
learningObjectives: Explain kernel state and execution-order hazards
Review notebooks for security and version-control quality
